QF.id: XIII Introduction to the Underlying Markets_69

question.text: Which of the following correctly ranks the three underlying markets by typical daily turnover in India (highest to lowest)?

answer.text: Forex market > Government securities market > Equity cash market
Equity cash market > Forex market > Government securities market
Government securities market > Equity cash market > Forex market
All three markets have approximately equal daily turnover

explanation.text: The Logic: In India, as in most major economies, the interbank/OTC foreign exchange market is by far the largest underlying market by daily notional turnover, well ahead of the secondary government securities market, which in turn is materially larger by notional than the equity cash market. The forex-largest, G-Sec-next, equity-cash-smallest ordering reflects the structural reality that FX is a global wholesale market and G-Sec activity is concentrated among institutional fixed-income participants. The Trap: The equity cash market gets the most retail and media attention, which leads many candidates to assume it has the largest turnover. That intuition is wrong on a notional-turnover basis, and the option claiming all three markets are roughly equal is also incorrect. Note: A clean ranked turnover comparison of Indian forex, G-Sec, and equity cash markets was not located in the cited workbook pages (Currency p.19, p.42; IR p.97, p.105; Equity p.134-p.136, p.140-p.141). The framing above is general Indian-market knowledge of relative market sizes rather than a workbook citation, and the numerical figures in any older explanation should not be treated as workbook evidence.
